### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **46** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6251f59051c0080bb1370f6ad792d4841a2ca307`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 37 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 42 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6251f59051c0080bb1370f6ad792d4841a2ca307` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `66262a6ae764e57aec4369f06705cfa70d60211a` — the merge of head `55663d72e68fe4fede0df09e69f6e09d9741a93a` into base `6251f59051c0080bb1370f6ad792d4841a2ca307`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 66262a6ae764e57aec4369f06705cfa70d60211a && git checkout 66262a6ae764e57aec4369f06705cfa70d60211a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6251f59051c0080bb1370f6ad792d4841a2ca307 55663d72e68fe4fede0df09e69f6e09d9741a93a && git checkout -B drift-repro 6251f59051c0080bb1370f6ad792d4841a2ca307 && git merge --no-ff 55663d72e68fe4fede0df09e69f6e09d9741a93a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6251f59051c0080bb1370f6ad792d4841a2ca307
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6251f59051c0080bb1370f6ad792d4841a2ca307` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Inputs: card #24895 (body; ruling A `6304380498`; claims `6331156452` and `6331438059`; seat call `6331411142`; dev reports `6331377734`, `6334379488`, `6336414029`), the cross-lane declarations (#6367 `6331420796` and `6334470965`; #22648 `6331427821` and `6334455088`; #6023 `6334465051`; #6017 `6334445279`), PR #25178's body, file list and `git diff origin/main...pr/25178` at this head (30 files, +1589/-103, merge base `e3aa111ad`), and the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) The write door — RIGHT, and exactly ruling A's narrowing.** `user_id: Field.lookup('sys_user', { required: false, searchable: true, deleteBehavior: 'cascade' })` mints no code. The refusal is the engine's standing reference check (`engine.ts` `assertReferencesResolve`: caller-supplied keys, non-system writes, `null`/`undefined`/`''` read as "no link", one `VALIDATION_FAILED` with a `reference_not_found` finding on the field; `mapDataError` answers 400). `'*'` and `usr_nobody` are refused by that same arm, on insert and on update; a real user and an empty User are accepted. The one residual is the engine's own and predates this PR: an `isSystem` writer passes the check (recorded on the check's own card); the PR's title test writes `usr_gone` that way and pins the title `null`, and the resolver treats such a row as an unrelated user, so it never reads as the admin-wide default. The same declaration is ALSO a widening, which the declaration line must carry: on `origin/main` the column was `required: true` (`:83`) and the display-title parity table pinned an omitted `user_id` as refused (`refused: ['user_id']`); at this head an absent, `null` or `''` User is accepted and means every user. Read in ② below.
- **(b) The resolver — RIGHT.** `isGlobalDefaultUser` reads `null`, `undefined` and `''` (the three spellings `assertReferencesResolve` skips) into one in-memory key `GLOBAL_USER = ''`; `resolveRow`, `resolveQuietHours` and `resolveDigest` all walk `[user, GLOBAL_USER]`; `WILDCARD = '*'` survives at `:163-164`, `:216`, `:227-228`, `:244-245`, `:259-260`, topic and channel only. No `'*'` tolerance remains: a stored `'*'` becomes `String('*')`, is not in `recipientSet`, and is dropped at the "ignore unrelated users" line, pinned with its control. `loadRows` passes no `expand`, so `r.user_id` is the raw id (the engine expands only when asked). Other readers of this object's `user_id` outside the resolver: none. `recipient-resolver.ts:251` reads membership rows; `organization-ownership-inventory.ts:522` lists the object by name only; the inbox and receipt `user_id` columns belong to other objects; the sibling objectui tree names the object in two tests that read neither `user_id` nor `'*'`.
- **(c) The boot conversion — RIGHT.** `engine.find` with `where: { user_id: '*' }`, `limit: 10000`, `{ isSystem: true }` and no tenant is a cross-organization system READ (the two-organization pin converts both); each write is `engine.update(..., { user_id: null }, { where: { id }, context: { isSystem: true, tenantId: row.organization_id } })`, one column on one row addressed by id, so it can neither merge nor delete a row. Idempotent: the second pass reads nothing, and `seen` ends the loop when every row read was a miss, so a kept collision cannot spin it. A collision is a refused write (`DUPLICATE_RECORD`, or `isUniqueViolationError`), the row stays as stored, and the boot reports once at `error` naming every row: ADR-0120 D4's refuse-never-keep-one, and the AGENTS.md level question answered rightly (the default has silently stopped applying). Its order against the index migration is immaterial: index first, and the `'*'`-to-empty write trips `DUPLICATE_RECORD` and is reported; conversion first, and two empty rows make the index migration refuse with `conflict` and list them. Loud either way, nothing lost. Armed at `kernel:ready` after the plugin's own provisioning hook, behind `typeof ctx.hook === 'function'`. The write site is the census-readable one the docs count: a same-file `const OBJECT: typeof PREFERENCE_OBJECT` with an inline context carrying `isSystem` and `tenantId`, generated as `preference-user-conversion.ts | update | sys_notification_preference | enabled | elevated | 1`, and the seven hand-written counts move by exactly that row (236 to 237, 159 to 160, 158 to 159, 177 to 178, 134 to 135, 195 to 196 typed receivers, 50 to 51 const-named); the measurement commit `452e9963c` is an ancestor of this head. `messageOf` over `operatorFacingErrorText` is right: no raw-SQL seam on this path. One edge noted, not a defect: a 10 000-row page whose rows are ALL misses ends the loop before a later page; admin-authored rows never reach that count.
- **(d) The NULL-safe index — RIGHT, a faithful copy of the `sys_setting` paradigm.** Key `(organization_id, COALESCE(user_id, ''), topic, channel)`, no `WHERE`, under the DECLARED name `uniq_sys_notification_preference_a22d7d27` (pinned driver-side on `main` as that declaration's replacement name, and present in both 18.0 fixtures), so `syncDeclaredIndexes` skips it by name and `isSyncReproducibleIndex` (an expression index whose fold is not the tenant column) marks it runtime-managed for the drift differ. Probe-first through `probeThenReplaceIndex`: the probe index is built before anything is dropped; `conflict` (`isUniqueViolationError`) leaves the previous index enforcing and no row touched, with the listing query and `os migrate duplicates` named at `error`; `unsupported` (MySQL's syntax refusal) likewise at `error`; `readTablePresence` `absent` is the silent no-op, `unreadable` is reported, `no-answer` proceeds exactly as `sys_setting`'s `tableIsPresent` rules. Armed inside the existing `shouldRunPlatformMigrations(...)`-gated `kernel:ready` handler with its own try/catch, and the new armed test pins both arms. The table exists before `kernel:ready` (`ObjectQLPlugin.start()` syncs registered schemas), so the first boot builds it too. It enforces one global default per (organization, topic, channel) on SQLite and PostgreSQL; NULL and `''` are one bucket (pinned); MySQL/MariaDB and driver-memory keep the declared NULL-distinct shape, the paradigm's documented reach. The roster grows to four in `runtimeIndexProbes()`; `duplicates.ts` consumes `collectRuntimeIndexPreflight` from the library, so the cli source is rightly untouched and `reportVersion: 2` rightly unchanged (a row, not a shape).
- **(e) `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'` — RIGHT, and ruled.** The seat call `6331411142` declares it as an execution parameter of ruling A from the measured M4 (under `set_null` a deleted person's own mute became the row that now means everyone), with the maintainer's veto kept. The engine honours it: a `lookup`'s delete behaviour is `fdef.deleteBehavior || 'set_null'` (`engine.ts`, the resolution near `:20030`), so `cascade` deletes the dependent rows on a single-id delete, and the REST bulk door (`deleteManyData`) deletes per id, so it cascades too. A predicate or `multi` engine delete skips cascade (logged) and leaves a dangling id, which the resolver ignores as an unrelated user: that is not the set_null widening. The registry row's claim that cascade closes that widening is correct.
- **(f) The registry row's `scope` — RIGHT by the registry's own test** ("does this property gate access"). An empty User widens the RANGE a delivery toggle covers (which users), grants no read or write, is overridden by a user's own row and bypassed by mandatory topics: the `scope` definition ("selects a range of work, not an access decision"), not `open` ("an access gate that is default-OPEN on purpose"). `evidence` is optional for `scope` and harmless. The declaration on #6017 invited a reclassification before enqueue; the spec seat's later stand-down brief on #6017 lodges none.
- **Other movement, named.** `runtimeIndexProbes()` (exported from `metadata-protocol`) returns four rows, read by `os migrate duplicates`; `ensureNotificationPreferenceIdentityIndex` and `convertWildcardPreferenceUsers` are NOT barrel-exported (no `index.ts` moves). Translations: the `en` leaves follow the source, and three retranslated leaves with their digests dropped from the source-hash files is merge mode's shape. `plugin.ts`: the import and one try/catch block, nothing else, as declared on #6367. The dogfood fixture's runtime-managed set (`sys_setting`, `sys_notification_preference`) is the right exclusion.

### ② Semver level

- **First word: `yes` is right; `no` would be wrong.** `clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes (narrowing)` as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; both facts are true and both are read". This diff does both: it narrows the write accept set (`'*'` and any id no `sys_user` holds are refused) AND widens it (an absent, `null` or `''` User, refused on `main` by `required: true`, is now accepted and meaningful). The dispatch-gates `--tier` note and AGENTS.md step 3 bind a card that ONLY narrows to `Clause-②: no`; this card does not only narrow, so that premise is unmet, and ruling A item 3's spelling (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`) stands on the facts, not on the ruling alone. The `(narrowing)` arm carries the BREAKING reading for `check-adr-0087-registration`.
- **Kind: `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.** Nothing an author writes moves: no spec key, accepted value, metadata type, default or meaning in `packages/spec/src`; the authorable-surface and authorable-defaults shards are untouched. What moves is a platform object's shipped field definition (`sys_notification_preference.user_id`) and the accept set of its DATA rows: #25105 ruling A row ④ (services, `fix!:`).
- **Level: `patch` on both moved packages, with the `**BREAKING**` banner, the FROM and TO, the operator fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker** (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category the gate lists): #25105 ruling A, "a non-protocol narrowing ships as `patch` but keeps its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition". `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on this head.
- **The full dogfood battery: STANDS, WITH ONE NAMED RESIDUAL.** Read from the code, this PR adds to a boot one catalog presence read, the probe-first DDL (drop-probe-if-exists, create probe, drop probe, drop declared, create declared: six statements over an empty or near-empty table, the shape `sys_setting`'s migration already pays on every boot), and one filtered `SELECT` with `limit 10000`. On the showcase's SQLite that is milliseconds against a 10 s hook budget that has to hold a full showcase boot plus sign-in, a budget the file never declares (its `beforeAll` awaits `bootShowcase()` and `stack.signIn()` with no timeout argument) while `showcase-scope-depth*.dogfood.test.ts` give the same boot `120_000`. So (i) is the file's budget, not this change's cost; it failed identically on `f7ad7e74b` and passed in isolation on `d272b23af`, and the cost bound settles the attribution without the no-change control the dev does not have. (ii) `object-designer-field-reorder` is a 5 s test over `saveDraft` plus `publish` on `sys_metadata`, a path no hunk of this diff touches. The two `upgrade-18x-index-equivalence` reds on the earlier head were this change's and are fixed and declared (#22648 `6334455088`). No re-run is owed. The residual, named: the showcase file's hook budget is an over-10-s test reproduced in two batteries and filed "carrier: none"; under AGENTS.md it is its lane's card, which the seat files outside this PR.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Stale QA checklist line** (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/integration-system.json:1668`, the `source` annotation "'*' wildcards + admin-global default"): ESCALATED, not a blocker. The topic and channel half stays true, the user half is stale; the file is not governed and was outside the claim; the carrier is a docs-only follow-up by the services seat (one annotation), never a rider on this PR.
- **ADR-0030's history row** (P2 "admin-global `*` defaults"): ANSWERED. A governed surface recording a landed decision's history; touching it would make the PR Tier H for no decision. Left as is, rightly.
- **`sys_notification_delivery.display_title`** (`channel` then `recipient_id`): ANSWERED for this PR, which ruling A item 5 excludes, and ESCALATED to the seat: no card naming it was found among the issues updated since 2026-10-20 (300 read, PRs excluded), and item 5 makes it the seat's own filing.
- **MySQL/MariaDB and driver-memory keep the NULL-distinct index**: ANSWERED. Identical to the `sys_setting` paradigm's reach (ADR-0120 D3 and D4); the MySQL arm reports at `error` with the consequence and the listing query, the changeset tells the operator, and driver-memory is no SQL host. No new gap opens.
- **Dev-report deviations, each closed**: the dogfood fixture and the census docs outside the claim are declared since (#22648 `6334455088`, #6023 `6334465051`); the registry row carries its full rationale (#6017 `6334445279`); `runtime-index-preflight.ts` and the driver-sql fixture are declared (#6367 `6334470965`); `duplicates.ts` is untouched by design; the four body sentences the dev could not patch are in the body now (the "Declared since" list, the registry section, the `messageOf` note, the final-head battery). `origin/main` carries 15 commits past the merge base, none on a file of this diff; the queue rebuilds the merge.
- **Check-runs on this head, read at write time**: every required context `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and its six shards, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`); `Check Changeset` `success` on both of its runs; the full-battery jobs `skipped` by event, as on every PR.
